newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-AJAX'S DANI HELPS BURY RANGERS CUP HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX'S DANI HELPS BURY RANGERS CUP HOPES.

text.p: Portuguese striker Dani scored twice to propel Ajax Amsterdam towards a 4-1 win over Glasgow Rangers, who had England's Paul Gascoigne sent off in the first half of the European Champions' League clash on Wednesday.
Dani's first half goals and further strikes by Tijani Babangida and Nordin Wooter in the final seven minutes enabled the Dutch side to celebrate their 100th European Cup match in style.

The result effectively killed off Rangers' hopes of making it past Group A of the Champions' League and into the last eight of the European Cup. It was the Scottish champions' 11th consecutive defeat in 3-1/2 years in the competition.

But it gave 1995 European champions Ajax a share of the lead in the group -- level on points with Auxerre and Grasshopper Zurich with two wins in three games -- and back on course for reaching the final for the third successive season.
And it brought a smile back to the face of coach Louis van Gaal. "We are not there yet," said Van Gaal, who described Dani as "an exceptional player" beginning to find his way in the Ajax system.

A floated cross in the 25th minute from Nigerian international Babangida on the right found Dani on the edge of the penalty area rising above the Rangers defence to send a powerful header past the outstretched right hand of goalkeeper Theo Snelders.
Ajax were given an extra boost three minutes later when Gasgoigne was sent off for kicking out at Winston Bogarde after coming off second best in a tussle with keeper Edwin van der Saar.

Rangers, reduced to 10 men, seemed to open up even more readily in defence. In the 41st minute Marc Overmars ghosted down the left and whipped a cross into the path of Dani, who headed past Snelders for his second.
Dani was denied a first-half hat-trick when a thundering drive from just outside the penalty area cannoned of the crossbar.
Rangers had to soak up more pressure in the second half but Ajax did not score again until the 83rd minute when Babangida found himself in front of an open goal and made it 3-0.
Rangers came back in the dying minutes getting a consolation goal in the 88th minute through Ian Durrant, who had come on minutes earlier as a substitute for Ferguson.
But in the final minute Wooter, who came on for Dani in the 78th minute, made it 4-1 for Ajax.
"I am very happy we won. We scored four goals against Rangers which is something special," Dani said. "We scored four, we are on the way back."

Ajax Amsterdam: 1-Edwin van der Sar, 2-John Veldman, 4-Frank de Boer, 5-Winston Bogarde, 6-Ronald de Boer, 7-Tijani Babangida, 11-Marc Overmars, 14-Martijn Reuser (8-Richard Witschge 42), 19-Arnold Scholten, 20-Marcio Santos, 21-Dani (16-Nordin Wooter 78).

Glasgow Rangers: 1-Theo Snelders, 2-Alex Cleland, 3-Joerg Albertz, 4-Richard Gough, 6-Joachim Bjorklund, 7-Stuart McCall, 8-Paul Gascoigne, 11-Brian Laudrup (17-Peter van Vossen 81), 20-Derek McInnes (16-Charlie Miller 81), 23-Craig Moore, 24-Ian Ferguson (14-Ian Durrant 85).
